title: 6515--WLR MRI IV Pump (VA-27-00019040)
description: Revision: 01 Effective Date: 11/15/2024 Acquisition ID#36C252-27-AP-0957 Page 1 of 2 Please note that this is not a request for proposal nor a request for quote as there is no solicitation document available. Therefore, this is a notice of intent issued by the Department of Veterans Affairs to negotiate a limited source contract with Iramed Corporation. DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS Justification for Single Source Awards RFO FAR 12.102 For Over Micro-Purchase Threshold but Not Exceeding the SAT ($250K) Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C252-27-AP-0957 Contracting Activity US Department of Veterans Affairs Great Lakes Acquisition Center (GLAC) VISN 12 115 S. 84th Street Milwaukee, WI 53214 2237: 556-27-1-2993-0011 Brief Description of Supplies/ Services required and the intended use/Estimated Amount: The Captain James A. Lovell Federal Healthcare Center (FHCC), Building 556, Nursing Services, is requesting the acquisition of one MRI-compatible IV infusion pump system for the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). MRI-compatible infusion pumps are medically necessary for ICU patients who require continuous vasoactive or sedative titratable infusions while undergoing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to support the diagnosis and evaluation of complex disease processes. Estimated Amount: $105,270.20 Unique characteristics that limit availability to only one source, with the reason no other supplies or services can be used: The availability of this equipment will enable FHCC to perform medically necessary MRI examinations on-site, reducing the need to transfer patients to outside facilities. Currently, these patients are often taken for CT scans; however, CT imaging may not provide the comprehensive diagnostic information required for certain conditions Standardization and compatibility with the MRI IV infusion equipment currently installed at the facility are essential requirements for this acquisition. The requested system is intended to integrate with the existing equipment and support established clinical workflows, training, maintenance, and operational procedures. Substituting products from another manufacturer could result in incompatibility, require additional accessories or system modifications, necessitate staff retraining, and increase costs to the facility. Therefore, procurement of the compatible MRI IV Infusion Pump System is justified to maintain system continuity, operational efficiency, and patient-care capabilities. Description of market research conducted and results or statement why it was not conducted: Market Research Findings: An SBA.gov search under NAICS code 339112 identified zero (5) SDVOSBs and (13) VOSBs. Two additional searches were conducted on sba.gov by combining NAICS code 339112 with the keywords Quad Non-Magnetic IV Pump System and Non-Magnetic IV Pump System and applying specific filters for SDVOSBs and VOSBs. Both searches yielded zero (0) results. A search on GSA Advantage using the keywords Non-Magnetic IV Pump System produced several results that does not appear to meet the requirement. The Contracting Officer (CO) searched Google.com using the keywords Non-Magnetic IV Pump System and identified several vendors, including BD, BioSpace, Hospital & Healthcare management, Iradimed, InMed, MDPI, and Ivenix. Although several alternative vendors were identified, their products are not compatible with the MRI IV infusion equipment currently installed at the facility. Standardization and compatibility are essential requirements for this acquisition. The requested system is designed to integrate with the existing equipment and support established clinical workflows, training, maintenance, and operational procedures. Substituting products from another manufacturer could lead to compatibility issues, require additional accessories or system modifications, necessitate staff retraining, and increase facility costs. Therefore, procuring the compatible MRI IV infusion pump system is justified to ensure system continuity, operational efficiency, and uninterrupted patient-care capabilities. CO received a letter of authorization from the vendor that certifies Iradimed Corporation is the sole manufacturer and authorized seller of the MRidium 3870 MRI Infusion System and its accessories. Due to proprietary considerations, Iradimed Corporation is also the exclusive source for replacement parts for the MRidium MRI Infusion Pump System. The MRidium 3870 MRI Infusion System is the only nonmagnetic, MRI-compatible IV infusion pump currently available on the market. Contracting Officer's Certification: Purchase is approved in accordance with RFO FAR 12.102. I certify that the foregoing justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief. Vernise L. Newton Contracting Officer

title: NX EQ Microscope Spine
description: The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Microscope: Spine product line as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as �national�) single Requirements contract award. The microscope provides a stable, maneuverable platform with motorized zoom and focus, long working?distance lenses, and high?intensity illumination suitable for deep spinal corridors. It supports hybrid optical/digital viewing, allowing the surgeon to operate through traditional eyepieces or external large?format 3D monitors. Integrated imaging capabilities provide 4K or higher?resolution video and still capture for clinical documentation, teaching, and intraoperative collaboration. Systems of this type include fluorescence visualization options (e.g., ICG (indocyanine green)?based vascular assessment), navigation data overlays, assistant viewing optics, and compatibility with surgical navigation platforms. The microscope is mounted on a mobile, counterbalanced stand or arm designed for smooth, low?effort repositioning during procedures. It includes OR?ready connectivity (HDMI/SDI), DICOM/PACS export options, and supports wireless data functions depending on configuration. This equipment is used in neurosurgery, orthopedic spine surgery, and related specialties requiring precise micro visualization during complex spinal procedures. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to meet all requirements for the solicitation. The objective is to provide Microscope: Spine throughout the VA medical centers and facilities located in the Continental United States (CONUS) or Outside of the Continental United states (OCONUS). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. (ii) The solicitation number is 75N98027Q00054. This solicitation is issued as a Notice of Intent (NOI) for a non-competitive combined synopsis/solicitation to award a contract or purchase order without providing for full and open competition (including brand-name, if applicable). This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 12.603, Streamlined Solicitation for Commercial Products or Commercial Services, and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Additional authority includes 41 U.S.C. 1901 and FAR 6.302-3(a)(2)(ii). The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions, intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a non-competitive basis to Krishagni LLC, 5528 Hennessey Ct, Apt 3N, Saint Louis, MO 63139 for onboarding the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) to the National Eye Institute�s (NEI) existing OpenSpecimen biobanking software instance and implementing associated Electronic Medical Record (EMR) integration services. Competition is restricted to Krishagni LLC because NHLBI�s requirement is specifically to onboard to NEI�s active, Krishagni-licensed and operated OpenSpecimen environment rather than to procure a separate standalone biobanking system. Acquiring a different biobanking product would not satisfy the requirement to join the existing NEI shared instance and would result in substantial duplication of software licensing, implementation, validation, and support infrastructure costs, as well as unacceptable operational delays. As the software developer, proprietor, and operator of the existing NEI OpenSpecimen environment, Krishagni LLC is the only responsible source authorized and technically capable of performing the required onboarding, workflow configuration, and EMR integration services within that shared platform. (iii) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026. (iv) The associated NAICS code is 541511 (Custom Computer Programming Services), and the small business size standard is $34.0 million. This requirement is not set aside for small business.

title: Call for Solutions - DeCA Ansbach Commissary Facility Maintenance
description: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) maintenance services for the commissaries within the Ansbach area. The prospective contractor shall provide a comprehensive preventative, unscheduled, and 24/7/365 emergency maintenance for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) services to ensure continuous operations and prevent inventory loss. Solutions should demonstrate rapid on-site emergency response capabilities, preventative maintenance compliant with local commercial standards, transparent fixed-price quoting and reporting procedures, and full compliance with applicable host nation (German/EU) statutory requirements and Department of War (DoW) statutory, safety, and warranty standards from firms operating in European Union, compliant with EU and host nation specific regulations and standards as it relates to commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) preventive maintenance and repair. Attached documents contain technical data that will provide assistance in understanding current conditions that the commercial solution will need to meet. Our objective is to establish a long term partnership with a provider whose technology, service model, and commercial terms align with our commitment to delivering reliable, value driven solutions. DeCA seeks solutions that will provide this support for up to five total years, requesting that solutions propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflect customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, use of CAFM systems, and repair benchmarks for the proposed support. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government's discretion. Please download the PDF documents attached to this call for solutions for additional details. The Call for Solutions Letter as five attachments on the PDF itself that contain important information to fully understand the complete nature of the call for solution.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTATIONS OR PROPOSALS This Notice of Intent is issued solely for informational purposes. The Government intends to award a sole source contract and is not seeking competitive quotations or proposals. No solicitation document exists for this requirement, and a Request for Quotation (RFQ) will not be issued. Intended Contractor SOVOS Compliance LLC 1055 Howell Mill Road NW, Suite 750 Atlanta, GA 30318-5557 Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Financial Management (OFM), requires the continued use of the SOVOS 1099 Pro tax reporting solution and associated Service Bureau services. The requirement includes the following software licenses: 1099 Pro Enterprise Desktop 1099 Pro 1042-S Pro W-2 Pro These licenses and associated services support NIH's annual federal tax information reporting responsibilities for payments made to vendors, contractors, foreign recipients, employees, and other reportable payees. The software must provide OFM with the capability to: Import and manage tax reporting data; Validate taxpayer and payment information; Prepare Forms 1099, 1042-S, and W-2; Process corrections and amended filings; Reconcile reportable amounts; Generate records in formats required for federal tax reporting; Electronically file returns with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) through the Information Returns Intake System (IRIS); Reprint recipient tax forms as necessary; and Support submission of corrected or replacement filings. The software must be deployable on NIH premises and support the printing of approximately 20,000 tax forms annually. The contractor shall ensure that all filing and mailing activities are completed in accordance with applicable IRS and Social Security Administration (SSA) deadlines and requirements. The software solution must maintain a FedRAMP Authorized designation at a level appropriate to the Government's requirements. Period of Performance The anticipated period of performance consists of one (1) 12-month base period: December 17, 2026, through December 16, 2027 Sole Source Rationale SOVOS Compliance LLC is the only known source capable of providing a FedRAMP-authorized version of the 1099 Pro tax reporting solution together with the integrated Service Bureau services currently utilized by NIH OFM. The SOVOS Service Bureau is an integral component of NIH OFM's tax reporting process because it provides the production and filing services necessary to complete the reporting lifecycle after OFM reviews and approves tax data. These services include: Printing and mailing recipient tax statements; Electronically filing applicable information returns with the IRS and SSA; and Supporting corrected and replacement filings, as required. Together, the 1099 Pro software licenses and Service Bureau services provide NIH OFM with an established end-to-end capability for preparing, validating, furnishing, correcting, and filing required tax information returns within statutory and regulatory deadlines. The SOVOS solution enables timely and accurate processing of large volumes of tax reporting data while maintaining continuity with existing NIH business processes and systems. Annual software updates are required to ensure compliance with changes to IRS and SSA forms, filing specifications, validation requirements, reporting thresholds, and electronic filing standards. These licenses and services must be renewed annually, and SOVOS releases updated versions each year to maintain compliance with current federal tax reporting requirements. title: International Recovery - Mexico (Follow-On)
description: Synopsis � 83310127Q0012 | Claim(s) in Mexico (Follow-on) EXIM Bank, headquartered in Washington, D.C., is providing this notice of intent to issue a sole source a follow-on award to provide asset protection and recovery services. The applicable Product/Service Code is R418. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541110 - Offices of Lawyers, which has a size standard of $16M. This requirement is to assist EXIM in its efforts to collect outstanding amounts owed to EXIM by the obligor/buyer and all guarantors, if any. These efforts will include, as EXIM may direct, asset searches, site visits, negotiations, litigation, documentation of agreements, embargoing assets and executing upon assets. See attached PWS. When an individual AMD recovery contract ends but the recovery action is still pending resolution, we award follow-on contracts on a sole source basis to the original vendor (per FAR 16.505(2)(c)) as long as it is for the same recovery case(s). The rationale for this is the combination of contingency payment agreement and the frequent long length of the recovery process. With limited vendor availability, if we did not follow this practice, the original vendor could perform most of the work and the subsequent vendor would reap the rewards of any funds recovered. By awarding follow-on contracts in this manner, we establish fairness for the vendors in an unusual situation, retain good relations with a limited vendor pool for future needs, and therefore get the best long-term benefit to the government. title: Sole Source to HII Unmanned Systems Inc for Hydroid Transponders and Assembly Per Attachments
description: This procurement is a Sole Source to HII Unmanned Systems Inc for for 10 Hydroid Transponders and Assembly The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Panama City Division, (NSWC PCD), Panama City, FL intends to award a firm-fixed price purchase order for HII Unmanned Systems, Mission Technologies Division brand products. Procurement is for SDV MK8 Hydroid Transponders, as follows: Line No. Description Part Number Quantity 1 ASSY; Transponder; CSS-LV; Aluminum; ID2 161907-2 10 EA 2 Associated Freight Costs FREIGHT 1 EA The Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) has a requirement to procure SDV MK8 Hydroid Transponders. This requirement is not suitable for full and open competition for the following reasons: This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 12.102, Restricting Competition. The determination has been made that only one source is reasonably available to meet the Government's minimum needs. HII Unmanned Systems is the OEM and the only approved source of supply for the items listed above per the approved engineering drawing. The purchase of a different brand of transponder would necessitate approximately 6 months or more of work to ensure compatibility of the alternate transponder with the SDV system. Additionally, further work would be required to approve it for use with the SDV system. The additional time and expense generated by these efforts would result in unacceptable risk to the project timeline and additional cost to the Government. As such, the government does not expect significant savings through competition and it is more advantageous to the Government to award on a sole source basis to HII Unmanned Systems for the items listed above.

(b) No counterfeit supplies or equipment/parts shall be provided. Counterfeit items include unlawful or unauthorized reproductions, substitutions, or alterations that have been mismarked, misidentified, or otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, unmodified item from the original manufacturer, or a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, including an authorized aftermarket manufacturer. title: Wire Rope Replacement Services at PSNS
description: Update: Interested parties may request a site visit to determine if they have the capabilities to provide this service 1) Window of Availability We can support a visit during normal day shift. 2) Base Access & Clearance Requirements - Security Requirement will be provides upon request 3)Foreign National Restrictions Restricted, no foreign nationals. 4) Point of Contact (POC) - Will be provided prior to site visit 5) RSVP & Cut-Off Deadlines -Must submit request prior to the close of this opportunity 6)Technical Constraints & Safety Gear Safety shoes and long pants. No photography. The Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS) Contracting Office (Code 400) is issuing this sources sought. The sources sought is being issued as a means of conducting market research to identify industrial capabilities that might exist in order to support an upcoming requirement for a Wire Rope Replacement Services contract. For additional information regarding the technical specifications, please refer to the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). Based on the responses to this sources sought, this requirement may be set-aside for small business (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition (unrestricted), the Government intent at this time is for a single award. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Telephonic inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, the Government will not be providing evaluations or comments to companies providing sources sought responses, but the responses will be used to inform the government as to the best means of procuring this requirement. Notice Regarding Sources Sought: This sources sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. This sources sought does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Navy is not seeking quotes at this time, nor accepting unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this source sought; all costs associated with responding to this source sought will be solely at the interested party's expense. Not responding to this sources sought does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM website (SAM.gov). It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Project Background This contract shall provide on-site wire rope replacement services for Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility, in Bremerton, Washington. This is a service to replace wire rope on seven (7) canes located at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard Additional details are provided in the draft PWS attached to this announcement (Attachment 1). Instructions to Submit Interest: Interested companies should submit, on company letterhead, a notice of interest including the name, telephone number, mailing address, and e-mail address of one point of contact. The notice of interest should include a brief description of your company and its capabilities as they relate to the requirements set forth in the notional PWS attached to this notice and include answers to the attached Request for Information (RFI) (Attachment 2). Please limit your response to no more than 5 pages. Please e-mail this information to the Government contacts listed below, with "Wire Rope Replacement Sources Sought Response N4523A27RPSNS" in the subject field, by the closing date of this notice. Angela Charpia, Branch Manager ,angela.m.charpia.civ@us.navy.mil Amanpreet Johal, Contracting Officer, amanpreet.s.johal2.civ@us.navy.mil Any applicable brochures or company capability material may also be submitted.

title: ICE Dallas Field Office Firearms and Tactical Training Facility Access
description: Instructions All Responses to this RFI/Sources Sought Synopsis must be sent to the following email addresses: Marland.Clark@ice.dhs.gov and Alfred.B.Mansaray@associates.ice.dhs.gov Introduction ICE is responsible for the detention, health, welfare, transportation and deportation of aliens in removal proceedings and aliens subject to final order of removal. The mission of Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) directorate is the planning, management, and direction of a broad program relating to supervision, detention and deportation of aliens who are in the United States illegally. In implementing its mission, ERO is responsible for carrying out all orders for the required departure of aliens handed down in removal proceedings, or prior thereto, and arranging for detention of aliens when such becomes necessary. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information for planning purposes and to determine appropriate strategies to meet the Agency's requirements. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a commitment for an RFQ in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this announcement and information submitted in response to this RFI will not be returned. Interested parties are instructed to submit the following information: (Note: Do not exceed 3 pages per RFI submission) POC information (name, title, phone number, address, email address, etc.) Socio-economic status Brief company capability statement addressing this requirement All business sizes and categories are encouraged to participate. All information received in response to this notice will be used to determine the appropriateness of set-asides for this requirement. The NAICS code for this type of service is 713990 - All Other Amusement and Recreation Industries. Requirement ICE is seeking the services of a responsible vendor that shall provide a secure law enforcement training facility to shoot and provide on-site tactical training on an annual basis. The facility shall be within a 60-mile radius of U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement & Removal Operations (ERO), 8101 North Stemmons Fwy, Dallas, Texas 75247, and must accommodate at least 200 ICE personnel per quarter for policy mandated firearms, defensive tactics, and corresponding policy review training. Please reference the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW) for further details. Due Date Responses from Interested Parties are due by 11:00am EST, Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Questions can be provided but will not be answered and will only be used to strengthen the SOW. Requested RFI Deliverables Contractor name, Contractor Business Size, Address, POC Contact (to include name, title, telephone number, email address, UEI, Cage Code, etc.). Contractors should specify their prior experience or contracts in the area. Specific feedback and comments on the anticipated capabilities and requirements stated above. Certification that the Contractor has the resources, capability, and willingness to meet the administrative and operational requirements outlined in the draft SOW. In addition to the general capabilities of interested contractors, ICE requests responses to the following inquiry: 1. After reviewing the RFI and attached draft SOW, are there any issues that should be addressed? All comments received will be gathered and reviewed.

title: USACE SPK DB Construction - Natomas NPP Named Pumping Plants - Sacramento, CA
description: USACE SPK requires a design-bid-build (DBB)construction services to renovate three (3) critical irrigation pumping stations - the Elkhorn, Riverside, and Pritchard Pumping Plants - located along the Garden Highway Levee in the Natomas region of Sacramento, California. The project requires removing existing discharge piping that currently penetrates through the levees and installing new discharge piping that traverses over the levees to connect to existing landside irrigation canals, as well as conducting levee excavation, backfilling, pavement restoration, and utility relocation. North American Industry Classification(NAICS) Code: 237110 - Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction. Product or Service Code: Z2NE Repair or Alteration of Water Supply Facilities. Small Business Administration (SBA) Size Standard: $45,000,000.00 Annual Revenue The target price range is estimated to be between $10,000,000.00 to $15,000,000.00 This requirement is without set-aside and pursued with full and open competition.

description: This Sources Sought Notice is not a Request for Quote and does not constitute a commitment by the Government. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 483114, �Coastal and Great Lakes Passenger Transportation.� The small business size standard for this NAICS code is 550 employees. This requirement is for resource protection and monitoring missions to the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands (NWHI) that supports requirements for the Papah?naumoku?kea National Marine Sanctuary (PNMS). title: Campbell VTG PM, Evaluation, Repair
description: The Commander Fleet Readiness Center (COMFRC) hereby gives notice of their intent to award a purchase order to Campbell Grinder Co., 1226 E. Pontaluna Rd, Spring Lake, MI 49456 (Cage Code: 18278) on a sole source basis. In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b)(2), only one source is reasonably available, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. FRC South West, NAS North Island has a requirement for necessary supplies and services to perform annual preventative maintenance (PM), evaluation, and repair for three (3) Government owned Campbell VTG Computer Numeric Control (CNC) grinding machines located at the Fleet Readiness Center Southwest (FRCSW). Campbell Grinder Co. does not authorize third-party field technicians and handles all maintenance, parts, and repairs entirely in-house. They deploy their own certified Local and Regional Service Technicians with proprietary knowledge directly to facilities for on-site PM, alignments, diagnostics, and repairs. Any government requirement for certified OEM maintenance or proprietary parts installation typically establishes a strong justification for a Sole Source Determination under FAR Part 13.5 or FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Responsible Source). For this reason, the Government intends to procure this PM, evaluation, and repair on a sole source basis from Campbell Grinder Co. (Cage: 18278). THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which, if received within three (3) calendar days after the date of the publication of this synopsis, will be considered. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement without impacting the requirement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The point of contact for this requirement is kelsey.l.herbert2.civ@us.navy.mil

title: ICE Dallas Field Office Shredding Services
description: Instructions All Responses to this RFI/Sources Sought Synopsis must be sent to the following email addresses: Marland.Clark@ice.dhs.gov and Alfred.B.Mansaray@associates.ice.dhs.gov Introduction ICE is responsible for the detention, health, welfare, transportation and deportation of aliens in removal proceedings and aliens subject to final order of removal. The mission of Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) directorate is the planning, management, and direction of a broad program relating to supervision, detention and deportation of aliens who are in the United States illegally. In implementing its mission, ERO is responsible for carrying out all orders for the required departure of aliens handed down in removal proceedings, or prior thereto, and arranging for detention of aliens when such becomes necessary. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information for planning purposes and to determine appropriate strategies to meet the Agency's requirements. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a commitment for an RFQ in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this announcement and information submitted in response to this RFI will not be returned. Interested parties are instructed to submit the following information: (Note: Do not exceed 3 pages per RFI submission) POC information (name, title, phone number, address, email address, etc.) Socio-economic status Brief company capability statement addressing this requirement All business sizes and categories are encouraged to participate. All information received in response to this notice will be used to determine the appropriateness of set-asides for this requirement. The NAICS code for this type of service is 561990 - All Other Support Services. Requirement ICE is seeking the services of a responsible vendor that shall furnish the labor, equipment, material, transportation, removal of shred bins to provide a once-a-month shredding for the Department of Homeland Security, Immigration & Customs Enforcement, Enforcement and Removal Operations, Dallas and its sub-offices at the in the attached Statement of Work (SOW). Please reference the attached draft SOW for further details. Due Date Responses from Interested Parties are due by 12:00pm EST, Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Questions can be provided but will not be answered and will only be used to strengthen the SOW. Requested RFI Deliverables Contractor name, Contractor Business Size, Address, POC Contact (to include name, title, telephone number, email address, UEI, Cage Code, etc.). Contractors should specify their prior experience or contracts in the area. Specific feedback and comments on the anticipated capabilities and requirements stated above. Certification that the Contractor has the resources, capability, and willingness to meet the administrative and operational requirements outlined in the draft SOW. In addition to the general capabilities of interested contractors, ICE requests responses to the following inquiry: 1. After reviewing the RFI and attached draft SOW, are there any issues that should be addressed? All comments received will be gathered and reviewed.

PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Design and Construction of four (4) Collective Training Enlisted (CTE) Barracks and one (1) Advanced Skills Training (AST) Barracks Location: Fort Hunter Liggett, California Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION This acquisition will deliver four (4) Collective Training Enlisted (CTE) Barracks and one (1) Advanced Skills Training (AST) Barracks at Fort Hunter Liggett, CA. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to demolish and dispose of five (5) existing Barracks and replacing with four (4) CTE Barracks and one (1) AST Barracks. Key features of the project may include: Design and construct four (4) multi-story CTE Barracks (approximately 46,000 total SF each), which will feature open bays, along with integrated officers sleeping rooms, team rooms, laundry facilities, restrooms, showers, storage, and janitorial closets. Supporting facilities may include but not limited to; site development, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, walks, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, HVAC, information systems, landscaping, signage, sustainability/energy, cybersecurity, and all required fixtures, furnishings, and equipment. Design and construct one (1) multi-story AST Barracks (approximately 45,000 total SF), which will feature sleeping quarters with bathrooms, study/day rooms, laundry rooms, storage, and janitorial closets. Supporting facilities may include but not limited to; site development, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, walks, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, HVAC, information systems, landscaping, signage, sustainability/energy, cybersecurity, and all required fixtures, furnishings, and equipment. The USPTO seeks innovative solutions to implement the next-generation biological sequence search system utilizing Super Intelligence (SI)-assisted capabilities to increase the efficiency and quality of biological searches during patent examinations. The USPTO is interested in solutions that meet the objectives outlined in the attached draft Statement of Objectives (SOO). The Government preference is to obtain a turnkey commercial solution with minor tailoring, if applicable. The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This PTAG Request for Information (RFI) is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the USPTO will use to determine which vendor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. Vendors that do not respond to the RFI will not be considered for the alternative competition and will not be eligible to compete as a prime offeror. Submission of an RFI response does not guarantee a vendor�s eligibility to compete for the biosequence search requirement. This PTAG RFI is not a request for competitive proposals. title: MACH1_AOI_Military Working Dog Facility_ Vandenberg Space Force_LOE 1 and LOE 2
description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is is executing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) project to renovate existing military working dog (MWD) facilities and construct a new addition at Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB), California. Under this agreement, the selected contractor will execute both the progressive design and physical construction to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant compound (Project Number: XUMU171121C). The current MWD kennel and admin facilities (Buildings 6444 and 6447) at Vandenberg SFB fail quarterly inspections and contain critical safety hazards that endanger military personnel and canine assets. Transitioning to a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model is critical to eliminate traditional design-bid-build delays, rapidly deliver compliant spaces, and preserve the security mission of the 30th Space Wing. There are (2) two distinct lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. title: FY27 HIOSH Hazardous Waste
description: The purpose of this amendment 01 is to provide a revise RFQ with a revised SOW. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) operates basic science research facilities in Cincinnati, Ohio; Morgantown, West Virginia; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; and Spokane, Washington. Each location generates hazardous, universal, and other regulated waste through research and laboratory operations. Each location is considered a Small Quantity Generator of hazardous waste. The approximate average monthly quantities generated are: Location Approximate Monthly Quantity Cincinnati, Ohio 100 pounds Morgantown, West Virginia 500 pounds Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 150 pounds Spokane, Washington 50 pounds Each location shall be treated as a separate job site. Hazardous waste shall be collected quarterly from designated collection areas. Contractor personnel shall not be required to enter individual laboratories. The acquisition is being pursued to obtain compliant collection, packaging, transportation, documentation, treatment, and final disposal services for waste generated at NIOSH facilities. The contractor shall provide complete cradle-to-final-disposal services and maintain the documentation necessary to demonstrate proper management of each waste stream. Performance shall comply with all applicable Federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including, as applicable, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Toxic Substances Control Act, the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Hazardous Materials Transportation Act, applicable United States Department of Transportation regulations in 49 CFR Parts 100�199, and applicable requirements in 40 CFR Parts 261 and 264/265. PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain safe, lawful, and fully documented management of hazardous, universal, and other regulated waste generated at four NIOSH research facilities. The contractor shall provide all personnel, labor, supervision, transportation, packaging, equipment, supplies, supplies, permits, licenses, analysis, documentation, and other resources necessary to: Collect waste from designated collection areas; Package and label waste for shipment; Prepare and process required manifests and shipping documents; Transport waste in compliance with applicable requirements; Determine appropriate treatment or disposal methods; Ensure waste is delivered to properly permitted facilities; Complete final treatment or final disposal; and Provide documentation and audit trails demonstrating the ultimate disposition of each waste item. The contractor shall perform all work in a safe, prudent, conscientious, and professional manner. Work shall be performed during NIOSH normal working hours and shall comply with all applicable safety, environmental, transportation, and security requirements. SCOPE OF WORK The contractor shall provide quarterly removal of listed waste streams for the Cincinnati, Morgantown, Pittsburgh, and Spokane NIOSH locations. Each site shall be considered a separate job for scheduling, pickup, invoicing, documentation, and performance purposes. The contractor shall not be required to enter individual laboratories. All hazardous chemicals waste, universal waste, additional waste listed below, and gas cylinders are not associated with all four sites. Waste may include the following: Hazardous chemical waste Flammable liquids, including alcohol, xylene, acetonitrile, and ethyl acetate; Non-pouring flammables, including gas cylinders, solids, and metal powders; Inorganic and organic acids; Inorganic and organic bases; Oxidizers; Solid metals and metal powders; U-listed and P-listed wastes; Peroxides and reactive waste; Mercury compounds; Non-RCRA solids and liquids; Dioxin; Pentachlorophenol and polychlorinated biphenyl waste; Flammable aerosols; Formaldehyde, formaldehyde solutions, and glutaraldehyde-containing tissue specimens; Small quantities of explosives, generally from 1 to 1,000 grams; Paints; Sodium cacodylate; Potassium cacodylate; Waste oil; and Used or expired self-contained self-rescuer cartridges. Universal waste Batteries; Pesticides; Mercury-containing equipment; Lamps; and Aerosol cans. Additional waste Used oils; Charcoal filters; and Aqueous waste. Gas cylinders Toxic, corrosive, flammable, oxidizing, or refrigerant gas cylinders; Majority of cylinders are high pressure steel, 9-10�D X 48-51�H Some cylinders in Pittsburgh have unidentified contents. Gas-cylinder removal shall be provided as a separate line item. The estimated quantities are: Location Estimated Cylinders Cincinnati, Ohio 0 Morgantown, West Virginia 10 Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 75 Spokane, Washington 15 Gas cylinders may be removed in one service event or over the life of the contract. Once removed, the cylinders are not expected to be replaced. The contractor shall provide lab-packs, drums, overpacks, packaging materials, labels, and other equipment necessary to safely consolidate, package, transport, and dispose of the waste. The contractor shall remain responsible for proper management of waste after it leaves NIOSH property, including transportation, spills, leaks, treatment, final disposal, and supporting documentation. TASKS TO BE PERFORMED Task 1: Provide Waste Collection and Packaging Services The contractor shall schedule and perform quarterly waste pickups at each NIOSH location. a. The contractor shall coordinate pickup dates with the designated NIOSH representative. b. The contractor shall collect waste from designated collection areas. c. The contractor shall not require access to individual laboratories. d. The contractor shall treat each NIOSH location as a separate job for scheduling and invoicing. The contractor shall provide all packaging and handling services required for safe shipment. a. The contractor shall supply lab-packs, drums, overpacks, labels, containers, absorbent materials, and other necessary packaging. b. The contractor shall package waste in accordance with applicable requirements. c. The contractor shall not require separation of tissue from formaldehyde solutions containing tissue. d. The contractor shall identify and manage incompatible waste streams appropriately. The contractor shall provide a separate line item for gas-cylinder removal. a. The contractor shall remove gas cylinders identified by NIOSH. b. The contractor shall manage cylinders with known or unidentified contents in accordance with applicable requirements. c. The contractor may remove cylinders during one service event or over the life of the contract. Task 2: Provide Transportation, Treatment, and Final Disposal Services The contractor shall transport waste in accordance with all applicable requirements. a. The contractor shall comply with United States Department of Transportation requirements in 49 CFR Parts 100�199. b. The contractor shall ensure that all approved subcontractors and transporters comply with applicable transportation requirements. c. The contractor shall ensure that shipping papers include required technical names, emergency-response information, and a 24-hour emergency telephone number. d. The contractor shall ensure that off-site shipments are properly labeled, marked, and placarded. The contractor shall provide final treatment and final disposal of all waste. a. The contractor shall send waste only to licensed, permitted, and approved facilities. b. The contractor shall ensure that each facility is authorized to handle the applicable waste streams and RCRA waste codes. c. Mere acceptance of waste at a treatment, storage, or disposal facility shall not constitute final treatment or final disposal. d. The contractor shall obtain documentation demonstrating completion of final treatment or final disposal. The contractor shall provide all required personnel, labor, equipment, permits, licenses, transportation, supplies, and services at no additional cost to the Government unless expressly authorized by the contract. title: Z1DA--Design Build | NRM 654-27-130 | Eliminate Trip Hazards Facility Wide VASNHCS
description: SOURCES SOUGHT DESIGN BUILD 36C26127R0011 This is a pre-solicitation notice under FAR 5.203(a), FAR 5.204, and FAR 36.601-1, and FAR 36.3 of the Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21 intent to contract for a Design Build Contract for the VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System (VASNHCS) Project No. 654-27-130, Eliminate Trip Hazards Facility Wide, located at VASNHCS, Reno, Nevada. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, and the small business size standard is $45 Million. A construction firm shall be responsible for both the design and construction of the project. This design effort includes, but is not limited to, providing Schematic Design (SDs), Design Development (DDs), Construction Documents (CDs), and Construction Period Services (CPS) necessary to perform construction to Eliminate Trip Hazards Facility Wide at VASNHCS. The contract work requires multiple disciplines for the design. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm. The disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Structural, Plumbing, Fire Life Safety, Sustainability, Security, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Way-Finding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Interested parties are advised that in keeping with the Veterans First Contracting program under 38 U.S.C. 8127-8128, as implemented under VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) subpart 819.70 and VA Procurement Policy Memorandum 2016-05 Implementation of the Veterans First Contracting Program, if the Contracting Officer has a reasonable expectation that two or more small business concerns owned and controlled by Service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concerns will submit responses to the solicitation and that award can be made at a fair and reasonable price that offers the best value to the United States, the requirement will be set-aside for SDVOSB concerns. If an SDVOSB set-aside is not appropriate, the requirement will be evaluated to determine whether a Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) set-aside is appropriate. The term SDVOSB / VOSB under the Veterans First Contracting program has the same meaning as defined in FAR subpart 2.101, except for acquisitions authorized by 38 U.S.C. 8127 and 8128 for the Veterans First Contracting Program SDVOSB and VOSB concerns must be listed as verified in the SBA Small Business Search (SBS) database at https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ in addition to meeting the NAICS code small business size standard to be eligible for award under Veterans First Contracting Program set-asides. Interested parties are encouraged to provide the following capability information to the Contract Specialist, Nicole Renfrew, via email at Nicole.Renfrew@va.gov by 10:00 A.M. Pacific Standard Time on November 17, 2026. Please complete the attached form with the following information: Business Size (Large/Small) Business Socio-Economic Status (SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, 8(a), HUBZone, etc.) Copy of current SAM record SAM Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number Copy of SBA SBS record showing verified status: SDVOSB/VOSB concerns only. Bonding Capacity: Provide your surety name, your maximum bonding capacity per project and your aggregate maximum bonding capacity. The bonding capacity per project must be $5 Million to be deemed acceptable for this notice. The Government will use this information when determining its business set-aside decision, taking into consideration the requirements outlined in VA Procurement Policy Memorandum 2016-05 Implementation of the Veterans First Contracting Program. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be issued on or about December 01, 2026. It is the intent of the Government to make a single firm-fixed price Design Build contract award for this requirement. Questions regarding this Sources Sought notice should be directed, in writing, to the Contract Specialist Nicole Renfrew, via email at Nicole.Renfrew@va.gov. This synopsis is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government and no contract will be awarded as a direct result of this Sources Sought announcement. title: Synopsis/Pre-Solicitation Notice for Joint General Mechanics Tool Kit (JGMTK), NSN: 5180-01-605-5146
description: This is notice that the U.S. Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) intends to solicit for the following requirement: JOINT GENERAL MECHANICS TOOLKIT: National Stock Number: 5180-01-605-5146 Part Number: 0694A0000 First Ordering Period: 21,492 EA (Estimated) Second Ordering Period: 6,300 EA (Estimated) Third Ordering Period: 6,300 EA (Estimated) Fourth Ordering Period: 6,300 EA (Estimated) Fifth Ordering Period: 6,300 EA (Estimated) The forthcoming Invitation for Bids (IFB) will be a Sealed Bidding Effort for Full and Open Competition and is anticipated to result in the award of a Firm-Fixed Price Five-Year Requirements Contract. This is a pre-solicitation notice / synopsis only. It is neither a request for competitive bids nor a solicitation of offers. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice. The content of any future IFB shall take precedence over all information contained herein. Once the IFB is issued, all responsible sources may submit a bid which will be considered by the agency. There is a Technical Data Package (TDP) associated with this procurement. The TDP is distribution statement "A", which is approved for public release. TDP access will be granted prior to IFB issuance. The forthcoming IFB will also contain instructions on how to access this technical data. The IFB, and any subsequent amendments thereto, will be issued electronically to the System for Award Management (SAM) website. The Government will not maintain an interested vendor mailing list. Therefore, it is incumbent upon any interested party to obtain the IFB and any amendments from SAM. Failure to obtain any amendments, and to respond to them prior to the date and time for receipt of bids, may render your bid nonresponsive and result in its rejection.
